newsitem.title: USA: No deal yet between WHX and striking union.
newsitem.headline: No deal yet between WHX and striking union.

text.p: Despite reports to the contrary, no tentative contract agreement has been reached between WHX Corp and the United Steelworkers union, union officials said Monday.
"There was no tentative agreement," union spokesman Charles Robideau told Reuters. "That was somebody's fantasy."
Negotiators for the two sides, including WHX Chairman Ron LaBow, have been meeting daily in New York since last Wednesday and were scheduled to meet again today.
Weekend reports said a tentative deal had been struck, but Robideau said that was false.
"They must be making progress since they're still talking," he said. "But what that progress is, I can't tell you."

Some 4,500 union workers have been on strike against WHX since last October, making the dispute the longest in steel industry history. The strike has idled eight steel plants in Pennsylvania, West Virginia and Ohio.

The strike centers around pensions. The union is demanding the company establish a defined benefit plan, which would guarantee that a certain amount of money is contributed to a worker's plan each month.

WHX maintains that it cannot afford such a plan, and instead has offered to enhance its existing defined contribution plan. Under that plan, a certain percentage of a worker's pay is contributed to an investment pool and pension payouts depend on how the pool performs.
James Bowen, the union's chief negotiator, met with local union presidents in Pittsburgh over the weekend to update them on the talks in New York.
"But he was emphatic that there was no tentative deal," Robideau said.
